programme.title: Timeshift
programme.sub-title: Bouffants, Beehives and Bobs - The Hairstyles That Shaped Britain
programme.desc: A look at the story of the iconic hairstyles that defined postwar Britain, from the meringue-like confections of Raymond `Teasy Weasy' Bessone, to the `architectural' precision cutting of Vidal Sassoon, via the bouffant, beehive and bob.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: A look at deserts, which cover a third of the earth's land surface. From space they appear lifeless but a closer inspection reveals a different picture. Deserts are in fact surprisingly varied, from Mongolia's Gobi desert, where wild Bactrian camels have to eat snow in lieu of water, to the Atacama in Chile where guanacos survive by licking the dew off cactus spines.

programme.title: I Am Martin Parr
programme.desc: Examines the work of contemporary photographer Martin Parr, known for his unique and intimate approach to his subjects.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: Although the frozen worlds of the Arctic and Antarctic experience the greatest seasonal extremes, it is the advance and retreat of the ice that is the real challenge to life. As the sea freezes, Antarctica doubles in size and all animals except for the Emperor Penguin flee. In the Arctic, the polar bear's ice world literally melts beneath its feet, forcing it to swim vast distances.

programme.title: The Good Life
programme.desc: Barbara starts to feel down about being an urban farmer, especially when a person walking by mistakes her for a boy, and ripping her last good dress seems to push her over the limit.

programme.title: Yes, Minister
programme.desc: Jim Hacker is outraged to discover that bribery was used to land a lucrative foreign contract. Meanwhile, Bernard is ensuring a gift from a foreign government can be undervalued to enable Mrs Hacker to keep it.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: The first of three films presenting a portrait of one of the world's greatest comic actors, tracing his life from childhood to a successful post-war career with the `Goons' and more.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: The second of three film portraits of one of the world's greatest comic actors. The years between 1959 and 1964 saw the peak of his career and his second marriage to Britt Ekland.

programme.title: Arena
programme.desc: The last of three film portraits of one of the world's greatest comic actors. In 1964, Peter Sellers was at his peak, with his films packing cinemas the whole world over, when a heart attack in California nearly killed him.

programme.title: The Trials of Oscar Pistorius
programme.desc: Six weeks into the trial of Oscar Pistorius, he takes the stand to explain what happened in the early hours of February 14th, 2013.

programme.title: Around the World in 80 Gardens
programme.desc: Monty Don visits the world's 80 most inspiring gardens. In Mexico, Monty visits the ancient water gardens of Mexico City and a surrealist fantasy garden hidden in the rainforest. In Cuba, he discovers a green revolution sprouting out of crumbling colonial lawns.

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: David Attenborough looks at the world's great plains, immense wilderness areas that seem empty, but which support the greatest gatherings of wildlife on earth, including two million gazelles on the Mongolian steppes, and three million caribou in North America. At the heart of all this is grass which is able to survive the baking savannahs of Africa, the frozen tundra of the Arctic, and the Indian floodplains.

programme.title: The Lost Neanderthals
programme.desc: The Mandrin Cave in southern France has been attracting the attention of archaeologists for 30 years. The cave was regularly occupied in prehistoric times, and a remarkable record of human habitation has been preserved by its soils.

programme.title: Natural World
programme.desc: At the jungle animal hospital in Guatemala, the wards are full of exotic patients, many of them orphans rescued from the illegal pet trade.

programme.title: Tribe
programme.desc: While living with the nomadic Darhad herders of Mongolia, Bruce Parry helps a migrating family move their livestock across a high mountain pass.

programme.title: Screen Two
programme.desc: Harold Pinter's screen adaptation of Franz Kafka's enigmatic masterpiece. The story of a man who gets drawn into a world of lies and corruption as he seeks to prove his innocence.

programme.title: Kafka Uncovered
programme.desc: Documentary in which novelist James Hawes attempts to demolish a number of myths and misconceptions about the life and work of cult writer Franz Kafka. The programme was filmed on location in Prague and Frankenstein in the Czech Republic.

programme.title: Timeshift

programme.title: Planet Earth
programme.desc: Tropical rainforests cover just three percent of the planet yet are home to a huge fifty per cent of the world's species. They are the richest environments on earth but also the most competitive. Travelling through this enchanted world it is possible to see the amazing strategies the inhabitants adopt in order to survive.

programme.title: Some Like It Hot
programme.desc: Joe and Jerry are two innocent musicians who accidentally witness a gangland murder. To get out of town in a hurry and be paid for it, they disguise themselves as women, and join an all-girl band travelling to Florida. All seems to be going well until Joe, as Josephine, starts to fall for Sugar Kane, the band's singer, and Jerry, as Daphne, elicits more interest than he'd like from millionaire Osgood Fielding III.

programme.title: The Life and Death of Peter Sellers
programme.desc: A biographical film about Peter Sellers' turbulent rise from popular BBC radio performer to one of the world's most gifted comedic actors. Propelled by an overly possessive mother, Sellers struggled to reconcile his relationship with women, celebrity and his many selves.

programme.title: Citizen Kane
programme.desc: Frequently voted one of the best films ever made, Orson Welles's masterpiece tells the story of newspaper magnate Charles Foster Kane in a series of flashbacks. A reporter is intrigued by the dying Kane's last word - rosebud - and sets out to find a new angle on the life of one of the most powerful men in America. Nine Oscar nominations resulted in only one award for the outspoken Welles - Best Screenplay.

programme.title: Talking Business
programme.desc: Ben Thompson looks at the impact of an uncertain jobs market on this year's crop of graduates and examines why many are starting their own businesses. LinkedIn's Chief Economist tells us why there's a 60 percent increase in start-ups and Ben also talks to a recent graduate who has just launched a cosmetic brand and serial entrepreneur Simon Squibb.
